flashcard_questions.q: Which historical campaign do the purges in Chapter Seven parallel?
Who are the first animals forced to confess in the yard?
flashcard_questions.a: The four pigs who had protested at the ending of Sunday meetings.

flashcard_questions.q: What do the dogs do to the four confessing pigs?
Which sensory quotation conveys the horror left after the executions?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘the air was heavy with the smell of blood’

flashcard_questions.q: Which quotation shows the dogs losing all restraint during the killings?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘the dogs had tasted blood, and for a few moments they appeared to go quite mad’

flashcard_questions.q: Which Soviet body do Napoleon's dogs represent?
Who led the NKVD during the Great Purge?
What lie does Squealer tell about Snowball's loyalties?
flashcard_questions.a: That Snowball ‘has sold himself to Frederick of Pinchfield Farm’.

flashcard_questions.q: Which quotation shows Boxer briefly doubting Squealer's account?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘I do not believe that. Snowball fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which line shows Boxer surrendering his own judgement to the leadership?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right’.

flashcard_questions.q: Which word means unfairly blaming one person for problems caused by others?
What reason does Squealer give for banning ‘Beasts of England’?
flashcard_questions.a: That ‘the Rebellion is now completed’, so the song is no longer needed.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is ‘Beasts of England’ genuinely dangerous to Napoleon?
flashcard_questions.a: It reminds the animals of the promises the revolution has broken.

flashcard_questions.q: Who composes the hollow replacement anthem for the farm?
What does Clover realise as she looks over the farm after the killings?
flashcard_questions.a: That terror and slaughter were not what Old Major's rebellion had promised.

notes: 15 cards: 6 theme or character to quotation, 4 context-to-relevance (Great Purge, NKVD, Yezhov, Minimus), 3 plot-event cards, 1 definition-front term card (scapegoating), 1 cause card (why the anthem is banned). Split the ban into the stated reason and the real reason rather than one stuffed card. Dropped terror, personification, forced confessions and propaganda as glossary cards — all four are demonstrated by the quotation cards, so a definition direction would interfere.
